name: Text2KGBench dbpedia_webnlg
licence: code Apache-2.0, data CC BY 4.0 (README text also says BY-SA - clarify)
unnamed_entity_mentions: ~0.1% of entity mentions; partial names only; no descriptions
how_it_could_serve_us: regression check that grounding does not hurt named-entity extraction

name: Text2KGBench wikidata_tekgen
unnamed_entity_mentions: ~10.2% of entity mentions, 17.7% of test sentences; 37/60 topic definite descriptions, 20/60 topic absent; 0/60 relational descriptions of another entity
how_it_could_serve_us: ready-made evaluation of topic-coreferent unnamed subjects ('The film ...'), needs document context; shows the phenomenon is frequent

name: WebNLG+ 2020 (v3.0)
unnamed_entity_mentions: expected ~0 (text verbalised from triples; consistent with the dbpedia_webnlg measurement)

name: REBEL
kb_or_ontology: Wikidata (220 most frequent relations in the paper's eval)
unnamed_entity_mentions: expected low: entities come from hyperlinked mentions (not measured)
how_it_could_serve_us: large silver training data for named-entity extraction; not for unnamed entities

name: TekGen (full)
licence: check (KELM release reported as CC BY-SA 2.0)
unnamed_entity_mentions: expected high: same construction as the Text2KGBench TekGen half, where 10% of mentions were unnamed
how_it_could_serve_us: large source of topic-coreferent unnamed subjects

name: KELM
licence: CC BY-SA 2.0 (reported by a later paper)

name: DocRED
unnamed_entity_mentions: low: annotated named mentions; 61.1% of facts need cross-sentence reasoning

name: AIDA-CoNLL (CoNLL-YAGO)
unnamed_entity_mentions: none: named mentions only; NIL = named but out-of-KB
how_it_could_serve_us: abstention / out-of-KB evaluation (complements our missing-fact case)

name: CoNLL-2012 (OntoNotes coreference)
unnamed_entity_mentions: includes nominal and pronominal mentions (to verify)
how_it_could_serve_us: detection of descriptions; no KB grounding

name: ISNotes
unnamed_entity_mentions: yes - bridging anaphors are descriptions tied to an antecedent ('the husband' -> Marie Antoinette), but no KB
how_it_could_serve_us: detection step of our task; small

name: BASHI
size: ~459 bridging NPs (344 referential), 50 WSJ texts (sources differ)

name: QALD-10
unnamed_entity_mentions: n/a - questions, not text; but 'the spouse of X'-type questions = our formalise step
how_it_could_serve_us: evaluate the description -> query step in isolation

name: LC-QuAD 2.0
unnamed_entity_mentions: n/a - but 1-hop templates give descriptions with gold answers on BOTH KBs
how_it_could_serve_us: source of test items: 'What is the spouse of X?' -> 'X's spouse', gold on two KBs
